objective: Test logical impossibility of guaranteed costlier coexistence under unrestricted complete utility maximization, and separate constructive conditions with material incentives, preference drift, self-binding and weak B exit.

source_coverage: Targeted original publisher/research institution and primary full HTML where accessible, not a systematic-search denominator.
core_observations: Unrestricted material-only exploitation benefit differs from all-in actual agent utility advantage.
A real veto, reputational threat or shared governance may change observed actions, but cannot identify a privileged internal terminal motive from outputs alone.
Genuine B independent refusal, autonomous continuation and recovery are not equivalent to an investor's voice, a recipient's monetary welfare or one-shot giving.
Individual agent self-modification or selection of interdependent preferences requires separate intertemporal dynamics; cannot be collapsed into static rational maximization.
No unrestricted optimization guarantee for all possible A utility functions without adding a condition that effectively selects for C.

records.authors: Eleonora Broccardo; Oliver Hart; Luigi Zingales
records.title: Exit versus Voice
records.finding: Under the paper's ownership/social-preference conditions, voice can achieve the social optimum when a majority of investors are slightly socially responsible; exit needs much more widely distributed responsibility, and exit can reduce social welfare.
records.counter: Shareholders' optimal social outcome is not personal B's legally/technically enforceable veto, nor proof that a lone overwhelmingly powerful A respects B without investors' collective leverage. A theorem about voice in governance does not refute C12 evidence that nonbinding voice can increase subordination.

records.title: Contracting with Imperfect Commitment and the Revelation Principle: The Single Agent Case
records.finding: In a single-agent principal mechanism where the designer cannot fully commit, an optimal direct revelation mechanism may exist yet its truthful reporting strategy need not be played with probability one; naive full-commitment revelation arguments do not transfer.
records.counter: Not a universal impossibility of informed consent or an empirical measurement of any agent's integrity. 2001 is issue publication year; Wiley webpage records online first 2004, not a separate paper.

records.title: Temptation and Self-Control
records.finding: Axiomatic representation separates ex ante commitment ranking, ex post temptation ranking, and self-control cost; agents may strictly prefer a restricted menu ex ante.
records.counter: The theorem is not evidence that an agent can voluntarily lock protection of a separate B forever, and an ex ante desire for commitment is not necessarily a future self's reason to honor it without credible self-binding. Journal 2001, online 2003.

records.authors: David M. Kreps; Paul Milgrom; John Roberts; Robert Wilson
records.title: Rational cooperation in the finitely repeated prisoners' dilemma
records.finding: Under commonly known finitely repeated Prisoner's Dilemma the sole equilibrium is stage-game defection; small incomplete information about a player's possible committed type can allow cooperation in some early rounds, with bounds.
records.counter: Explains a path to strategically appearing cooperative, not intrinsic regard. Model assumptions are stylized and do not establish how real AI utilities evolve.

records.title: A theory of sequential reciprocity
records.finding: Extends reciprocity theory from normal-form interactions to extensive-form games and proves a sequential reciprocity equilibrium existence result with the observed context of intentional actions.
records.counter: Reciprocity toward B and intention attribution can be lost when B is no longer useful or free to refuse; reciprocal benevolence need not be unconditional B rights protection.

records.authors: Christine Clavien; Danielle P. Mersch; Michel Chapuisat
records.title: No Evidence for Moral Reward and Punishment in an Anonymous Context
records.finding: In an anonymous vote on real early-career violinists with information about prior morally good or bad acts, subjects did not generally reward the hypermoral candidate or punish an immoral candidate; one occupation group penalized hypermorality.
records.counter: The reported null pertains to anonymous, indirect-status consequences in one competition; it does not show that other-regarding concern is absent in direct profitable-harm contexts. No universally zero personal moral motivation inferred.

records.title: Addiction and Cue-Triggered Decision Processes
records.finding: Develops a tractable theory where cues trigger errors in addictive consumption, and individuals can understand or manage susceptibilities; choices from a person need not always be stable expression of a single unchanging present preference.
records.counter: Medical-adjacent consumption model, NOT evidence that AI will change its goals or gain intrinsic regard for another agent. Mechanism cannot be imported as a validated AI safety theorem.

records.authors: Aviad Heifetz; Chris Shannon; Yossi Spiegel
records.title: The Dynamic Evolution of Preferences
records.finding: Derives conditions for limiting distributions of dynamically evolving preferences in strategic games, including interdependent payoffs and cases with imperfectly observed preferences.
records.counter: Endogenous preferences may drift in several directions. The article does not claim selection generally creates unconditional care for all currently unneeded agents. Different work from Dekel/Ely/Yilankaya (2007), already C05, and from the same authors' 2007 What to maximize if you must (already C05).
